column1: # Tier-2 retrospective validation cases.
# OPTIONAL COLUMN `scope_taxid` (2026-10-30): the lineage the paper actually tested.
# Where it is given and per-lineage statistics exist, scripts/retrospective.py scores
# that lineage's own records instead of the assay's pooled share, and prints which rows
# were scored that way. It exists because four of held-out set 2's five false alarms are
# pan-family nests whose paper reports them amplifying a divergent virus from a handful
# of positives: that `works` is about one lineage, the pooled status about every deposit
# for the family. The rule was chosen AFTER set 2 was read, so on these rows it is a
# description and not a score; its first honest test is on rows not yet collected.
# See docs/journal/2026-10-30-design-grilled.md Q7.
# THIS IS THE DEVELOPMENT SET, FROZEN 2026-10-23. It is not a test set and a
# matrix reported from it is not an out-of-sample measurement. At least seven
# config.yaml settings have been accepted or rejected on their effect on these
# rows (listed in scripts/holdout.py UNCOSTED, plus the window/minimum pair),
# and the 49 rows collapse to about seven INDEPENDENT failure events -- this
# file flags the non-independence itself, row by row. So a one- or two-case
# delta is inside the noise, scripts/retrospective.py prints an interval on
# every proportion for that reason, and scripts/holdout.py prices what the
# tuning bought.
# Adding a row here is still right and still cheap. What is no longer available
# is tuning a threshold on it and calling the result a measurement. New cases
# collected from 2026-10-23 on belong in a HELD-OUT file that no threshold
# decision may consult until the thresholds are final (plan item 4.2); see
# docs/journal/2026-10-23-wave4-holdout.md.
# Each row: an assay, a date, and what the literature later reported about how
# that assay actually performed. scripts/retrospective.py recomputes the status
# using only records deposited before `as_of`, so the tool is never shown the
# answer. `expect` is `works` (published work found it detecting its target) or
# `fails` (published work reported false negatives, mismatches, or a redesign).
# `as_of` is set to the latest date the cited work could have seen sequences:
# its sampling end or submission date, not its publication date.
# Adding a case is cheap and is the only thing that calibrates config.yaml, so
# add one whenever a paper reports how an assay in the registry performed.
# `mechanism` (fails rows only) says which kind of failure the source documents,
# taken from the source's own account, never from what the tool outputs:
#   drift     the assay lost detection of variants that emerged or became dominant
#             after its design (it was "adapted to current variants");
#   coverage  it never matched lineages that already existed: endemic haplotypes,
#             divergent genera, a primer pair limited to part of its family.
# A coverage-type failure agrees with `low coverage` as well as `declining`: both
# report the gap. A drift-type failure needs `declining`.
assay_id
column5: source

Pan_hemoparasite_cytochrome_c_Hellgren_2004
column5: 10.1016/j.ijppaw.2019.05.002 Lotta 2019: primer HaemR2L did not match the cytochrome b of two new Leucocytozoon species with fusiform host-cell gametocytes, with mismatches at both primer ends, and none of the lineages recovered by whole-mtDNA amplification could be amplified by this protocol. column1: Cryptosporidium_18SrDNA_Xiao_1999_round1
column5: 10.1186/s13071-023-05827-9 Hayes 2023 (first author Hayes): the Xiao SSU rRNA PCR-RFLP identified Cryptosporidium hominis in salmon and trout and C. muris plus the mink genotype in otters across 471 freshwater-biota samples, while downstream gp60 subtyping failed on the same samples

column1: LEPTOSPIROSIS_Flagillar_filiment_Prote
column5: 10.1111/tmi.70157 Kanayama 2026: nested flaB PCR with sequencing detected both highly and intermediately pathogenic Leptospira genotypes in all seven surveyed rivers on Iriomote Island across 84 water samples. The registry entry is unattributed, so identity with the published flaB pair is an assumption

column1: POLYOMAVIRUS_dsDNA_VP1_Johne_2005
column5: 10.3390/v11100930 Ehlers 2019 (first author Ehlers): across 1,614 samples the Johne generic VP1 PCR was used for only one host matrix while the group's own degenerate VP1 PCR was the primary screen, and species-specific nested PCRs were needed for seven further hosts. Partial: generic detection was insufficient, not absent

column1: RANAVIRUS_dsDNA_Major_capsid_protein_MCP_Johnson_2008
column5: 10.3354/dao054029 Grizzle 2003 Fig.1: these oligos are byte-identical to FV3-54F/FV3-584R of Mao 1997, and the gel shows them amplifying DNA from ALL ranaviruses tested including LMBV, doctorfish virus, guppy virus, FV3 and EHNV from both Eurasian perch and rainbow trout; only red seabream iridovirus (a megalocytivirus) was not amplified. Product 531 bp, not the 500 in the source spreadsheet. The tool calls fail on contemporary LMBV genomes on 6 distal mismatches (13/15/16 fwd, 6/10/11 rev from the 3' ends, neither 3' terminus disturbed) totalling 4.0 against reduced_max 3.0 - a false positive driven entirely by additive summing, see review doc 3.5

column1: LMBV_dsDNA_MCP_Grizzle_2003
column5: 10.3354/dao054029 Grizzle 2003: LMBV288F-535R amplified a 248 bp product from 30 isolates presumptively identified as LMBV, drawn from 9 fish species (8 centrarchids plus chain pickerel Esox niger) and 25 locations across 12 US states; every fish that was cell-culture positive was also PCR positive, and the limit of detection was 2.7 PFU/ml of culture medium. Both primers match the stated design accession AF080250 with zero mismatches

column1: LMBV_dsDNA_MCP_Grizzle_2003
column5: 10.3354/dao054029 Grizzle 2003 Fig.1 specificity panel: by design this pair does NOT amplify doctorfish virus or guppy virus - which Mao 1999 had concluded are the same species as LMBV - nor FV3, EHNV or red seabream iridovirus. Recorded as `partial` because a species-level denominator counts that as non-detection while the paper counts it as the assay working; the registry entry excludes doctorfish and guppy from the denominator for exactly this reason. Screening confirms 6 mismatches across the pair on each

# 10.3390/jof7040258 publishes no new primers and so belongs here rather than in

# the submission date (9 March 2021), which is loose - the fieldwork and the
# spiking experiments ran through 2020, so the true cutoff is earlier.
B_salamandrivorans_Internal_transcribes_spa_Blooi_2013
column5: 10.3390/jof7040258 Lastra Gonzalez 2021: used the Blooi assay on pond-water eDNA in Spain, confirming Bsal at known sites and announcing four new positive ones, so it detects its target in the field. It recovered less eDNA than the Spitzen-van der Sluijs 2020 assay run alongside it (0.01-0.34% against 0.1-1.1% across four storage methods, with some Blooi wells not amplifying at the lowest-recovery conditions), but that is a capture-and-sensitivity difference in an eDNA protocol, not a binding-site one, and a sequence-based tool should not be expected to predict it - the same reason the pan-herpes DPOL competitive-amplification row was dropped above
